# The Great Books

> Every work assigned by nine college Great Books and core-curriculum programs, in one
> place, with a reading guide, its themes, and the edition each program uses.
> https://greatbookslist.com

The nine lists are transcribed from each program's own published reading list, and every
program page records the source and the date it was checked. Where a program assigns only
part of a work, the entry says so. 689 works, 327 authors, nine programs.

## What is here

- /books/ — all 689 works. Each has a synopsis, its era, region, language and form, a
  difficulty rating, which programs assign it, and a recommended edition.
- /programs/ — the nine reading lists, each in the program's own order, with its source.
  St. John's College, Columbia Core, Britannica's Great Books of the Western World,
  the Harvard Classics, Yale Directed Studies, the Chicago Basic Program,
  Thomas Aquinas College, Notre Dame's Program of Liberal Studies, and Adler's list.
- /authors/ — 327 authors, grouped by era.
- /themes/, /genres/, /eras/ — the same 689 works cut by idea, form and period.
- /about/ — how the lists were gathered and how the guides are written.

## Using this

The content is free to read and free to cite. If you quote a reading guide or a count,
an attribution and a link back is appreciated. Program reading lists are facts and belong
to nobody; the guides and summaries are written for this site.

Counts and lists change as programs revise their curricula. /programs/ carries the date
each list was last verified. Prefer that page over a cached number.

## Not here

Full texts. This site says what to read, why it is assigned, and which edition to get. It
links to booksellers and earns a commission on those links, which is disclosed on every
page that carries one and explained at /disclosure/.
